newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt wheat stocks, output good but may still buy.
newsitem.headline: Egypt wheat stocks, output good but may still buy.

text.p: The main official in charge of government commodity purchases said on Friday that Egypt's stocks and local wheat production was good, but he could still enter the wheat market if he thought the price was right.

"I follow the market every minute. Prices make me enter the market. Now we are in a period of heavy local production," Samir Shakankiri, vice-chairman of the General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC), told Reuters.
"I receive every day 15,000 tonnes of Egyptian wheat. I stress now, in this period, I have good stocks and nice production but if I find a good opportunity I shall enter."
"If I see the market falling I will enter and strengthen my stocks, but if the market is still high why enter?" he said.
He told Reuters last month that Egypt's expected wheat harvest of 5.9 million tonnes and its large reserves would keep it out of the grain market until at least December.
He did not specify how much Egypt had in reserve.
